Team,

I'm pulling together notes for HC-1284 (Ravi Patel). Panel is split on whether to place on L5 manager track or keep as Senior IC. Quick summary and asks below — attaching the candidate resume and a preliminary comp comparison.

Why this is ambiguous:
- Candidate has run a 5-engineer team at previous company but title was informal ("tech lead").
- Strong product + execution signals; mixed signals on direct people management scope.
- Compensation ask ($210k base + equity) sits near upper quartile of L5 band depending on location.

Asks:
1) Can the committee sign off on an anchoring principle for this role: promotion-to-manager hinge or manager-track offer?
2) If manager track, do we align to L5-manager comp band OR extend a manager-designated signing bonus?
3) Any specific leveling criteria we should document for future ambiguous cases?

Attachments: candidate_resume_ravi_patel.pdf, comp_comparison_hc1284.xlsx

Proposed next step: 30-min calibration call tomorrow (Mar 9) — available windows: 10:00-11:00 or 15:00-15:30 PT.

Thanks,
Hannah

Hannah —

Thanks for the summary and attachments. Short thoughts from People Ops: 

- Guiding principle: title/level should reflect the scope of ongoing responsibilities, not just prior but isolated manager experience. If we expect the role to own hiring, performance management, and career growth for a team (ongoing), lean manager track. If management is project-based or mentorship without formal direct reports, lean Senior IC.

- For ambiguous cases we use three signals (documentable): 1) ownership of P&L or roadmap decisions that require direct headcount changes, 2) formal owning of performance reviews/hiring signoff, 3) prior track record of developing managers. Give 2+ signals => manager.

- On comp: L5-manager band for SF/remote-CA supports base up to $215k with med equity. If we want to be competitive and candidate is a manager in practice, we can offer L5-manager base + hire bonus (one-time) up to $15k instead of increasing base above band.

I'll join the calibration call tomorrow at 10:00 PT. Please also bring interview_panel_notes.pdf with specific examples that show scope.

Regards,
Laura
Laura Bennett
VP, People Operations

Adding the hiring manager perspective:

- I ran the on-site panel. Candidate clearly articulated roadmap ownership for the infra feature we need (KV cache persistence). I asked for examples where they'd hired and managed — they described a multi-quarter hiring plan and performance calibration; not HR paperwork, but they owned hiring decisions in practice.

- My read: candidate has de facto manager responsibilities today. If we expect them to run the team long-term, manager track is defensible. I'm concerned about scope creep if we hire as an IC and then ask them to lead a team.

- Suggested offer: L5-manager base $205k - $210k (depending on final comp comp), standard L5 equity grant, and a $10k sign-on bonus with a 12-month clawback. No immediate manager title change requirement — we can title them "Engineering Manager" at hire and set 90-day goals to formalize direct-report permissions.

Attached a short slide (interview_panel_notes.pdf) with pull-quotes from interviews.

If the committee wants stronger guardrails for future cases, recommend we add a short checklist into the hiring SOP: 3 signals above + explicit hiring-manager confirmation.

-Marissa

Thanks everyone for the notes and the call yesterday. Short decision for records: 

- Approve L5 (Manager) placement for HC-1284. Rationale: 2+ manager signals (owned hiring decisions; roadmap ownership; candidate comfortable with people management).
- Compensation: approve base up to $210,000 + standard L5 equity. Approve $10k sign-on as requested. If candidate pushes for higher base, allow Hannah to counter with an additional $5k one-time cash or small equity bump but do not exceed $215k base without Exec sign-off.
- Action items: Hannah to confirm offer with candidate and include the 90-day managerial onboarding checklist. Laura to update SOP with the 3-signal checklist and add a reference case. Marissa to prepare the 90-day goals for the candidate.

Thanks — steer the offer and let me know when it's accepted so we can start initial org onboarding.

Jonas Weber
